historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr / revenue_5yr_cagr (3.7% / 4.1%), cross-checked against FY2026 guidance of 4-5% constant-currency
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (14.1% 3-yr, 9.6% 5-yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (3.7% / 4.1%); IBM book value is driven by pension OCI swings and the FY2022 Kyndryl-related trough (22,021), not by retained operating earnings, so it is NOT the growth anchor. EPS CAGRs are meaningless: FY2022 EPS 1.82 sits on 3.2bn of Q3-2022 pension-settlement charges and FY2025 EPS 11.36 carries a 1.4bn Q4 tax benefit. 5-yr FCF CAGR (-8.2%) compares against FY2020, which still included Kyndryl's cash flows (spun Nov-2021); the 3-yr figure is the clean one.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes: FY2022 7,695, FY2023 11,151, FY2024 10,435, FY2025 9,369. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR 6.8% is materially below the reported-FCF 3-yr CAGR of 10.0%: SBC + withholding grew from 1,394 (FY2022) to 2,733 (FY2025), i.e. an increasing share of reported cash growth is being paid for in stock. Note also FY2025 owner FCF fell 10% on FY2024 while reported FCF was flat, for the same reason.

scenario_narratives.base: IBM grows 4.5% in FY2026 (guidance midpoint, Confluent included) and settles into 2.5-3.5% organic growth thereafter as Software (Red Hat, automation, data/AI, now ~44% of revenue) offsets a cyclical Infrastructure trough in FY2027 and a flat-to-low-growth Consulting franchise. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands ~1pp over ten years on mix. The valuation is dominated by the terminal value (15x cap binds) and by the 55bn of net debt that the Red Hat/HashiCorp/Confluent programme has built up.
scenario_narratives.bull: The generative-AI consulting backlog converts to revenue, Consulting returns to mid-single-digit growth, and Red Hat/HashiCorp/Confluent keep Software growing low-double-digits, so the group compounds ~5% for four years and the Software mix lifts margin 3pp. SBC glides down as the acquired teams settle. Terminal 16x owner FCF at 3% growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consulting stays flat while the mainframe cycle troughs, hyperscaler AI platforms erode IBM's share of enterprise AI budgets, and Software decelerates to mid-single digits; group growth 1-2%, margin down 1.5pp, SBC stuck above 4% of revenue, cash tax rising to 22%. Terminal 13x at 2% growth. Leverage is serviceable but the equity is a thin slice of a 270bn enterprise value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis expenses SBC (1.7bn) AND the cash withholding on vesting (1.0bn) as the real cost of keeping the share count flat; IBM has bought back no stock since 2019, so the flat count is paid for only in the flows. Growth is organic-ish after FY2026 and acquisitions are treated as value-neutral, so the model gives no credit for bought growth but also charges no M&A outflow. Interest income on the 7bn cash balance is left inside the margin anchor at a shaved 27.5% rather than stripped, because IBM is a net-debt company. The terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF (Gordon would give 20.5x) because IBM is a structurally slow grower; the cap, not terminal growth, sets the terminal value in every scenario, which is what keeps the WACC/g sensitivity tame.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value share: the 15x cap binds in every scenario, so the valuation is ~55% terminal; a 13x exit takes roughly 15% off base.
Leverage: 55bn net debt against a ~230bn enterprise value means a 10% EV change is a ~13% equity change; the balance-sheet date (30 Jun 2026) already absorbs Confluent but not any later deal.

SBC path: the 4.2% -> 3.5% glide assumes retention grants from HashiCorp/Confluent roll off; holding 4.3% flat is worth roughly -5/share. The street basis (SBC as non-cash) is the upper bound of the band.

Acquired-intangible amortisation (~2bn/yr) is inside D&A and mostly non-deductible; the cash tax path is calibrated to actual cash taxes to avoid overstating the shield, but a reader adjusting D&A without adjusting tax will move value.
Mainframe cycle: FY2027 is the z17 trough; the base path's 3.5% assumes Software and the z17 tail offset it. A deeper trough with flat Consulting is the bear path.
Reported vs. owner FCF: IBM's own FCF definition (excludes financing receivables, includes software capex) will print above the 12.1bn XBRL figure used here; do not read the gap as a modelling error.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 199.19-332.46.
data_sources.financials: IBM_Metrics.csv / IBM.duckdb core_metrics (SEC XBRL, FY2007-Q2 2026) for revenue, net income, OCF, PP&E capex, SBC, shares, debt, cash; SEC companyfacts API (CIK 51143) for pretax income, interest expense, depreciation, intangible amortisation, income taxes paid, equity-award withholding, diluted shares, lease liabilities and acquisition spend (FY2024, FY2025, Q1-Q2 2026 10-K/10-Q). Net debt and share count from the 30 Jun 2026 10-Q.
data_sources.qualitative: IBM_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): FY2026 guidance (4-5% cc revenue, FCF up ~1bn), segment trends, Q2 2026 results, bull/bear axes.

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2025 10-K: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 1,715 (cash-flow add-back) + us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 1,018 (financing outflow). IBM publishes no combined equity-award figure, so the two lines are summed. H1-2026 run-rate is 1,004 + 465 = 1,469 (4.4% of revenue).
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 weighted-average diluted shares (us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, 953.26M; cover-page basic 942.13M at 30 Jun 2026). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. IBM has repurchased no stock since FY2019 (Red Hat deleveraging), so the count has drifted up ~1.5%/yr on grants -- the flat count is a modelling convention the company is NOT currently funding with buybacks; the SBC charge in the flows is what pays for it.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10-yr UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.8 -> cost of equity ~8.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (FY2025 interest 1,935 on ~60bn average debt gives 3.2% embedded, but new issuance is ~5%), after-tax ~3.9%. Market weights ~77% equity (210bn cap) / 23% debt (62bn) give ~7.2%; rounded UP to 7.5% for the mainframe-cycle lumpiness and the 3.4x net-debt/EBITDA leverage post-Confluent. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not charged again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating leases stay inside the flows (FY2025 operating lease payments 1,011 are opex inside EBITDA); operating lease liabilities (3.3bn) are NOT in net debt. Finance lease obligations (~1.15bn) sit inside reported total debt and are deducted once there; capex_pct is set at 2.9% (above the 1.6% PP&E + ~1.0% software cash lines) to cover finance-lease-funded data-centre assets (280/yr principal) so those are charged once, in the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is 89 at 30 Jun 2026 -- immaterial, ignored. Financing segment (~1% of revenue): its income is inside EBIT and its funding (financing debt) is inside the 61,984 total debt deducted in the bridge; the ~7-8bn financing-receivables book is therefore NOT added back as a separate asset (that would count it twice against the income already in the flows). This slightly understates value (receivables yield below WACC are capitalised at WACC) by an amount too small to matter at this size.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1, operating company -- diversified enterprise software/consulting/infrastructure; the financing arm is ~1% of revenue and is folded in as above rather than split out, per the straddle rule only warranting a sum-of-parts when the second business is material). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Revenue base FY2025 67,535 EXCLUDES Confluent (~1.1bn revenue, closed Q1 2026 for ~10.5bn cash): the purchase price has already left the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet (cash 13,587 -> 7,172), so FY2026 growth of 4.5% (guidance 4-5% cc, FX neutral, H1-2026 +4.9%) carries the acquired revenue against a net-debt figure that has already paid for it. IBM is a serial acquirer (8.3bn FY2025, 10.5bn H1-2026); no M&A allowance is in the flows and later-year growth is set at organic-ish 2.5-3.5%, so acquisitions are treated as value-neutral (paid at fair value) rather than a free growth source. Reported FCF here is the XBRL OCF - PP&E capex (12,102); IBM's own FCF definition excludes financing-receivable movements and includes software capex, and is higher. EBITDA margin anchor: FY2025 pre-SBC EBITDA 18,999 = 28.1%, but that includes ~0.4-0.5bn of interest income on cash and a Q4-heavy year; FY2026 is anchored at 27.5% (H1-2026 25.6% vs H1-2025 25.4%, +0.2pp). D&A (7.4% FY2025, 7.9% H1-2026) is dominated by acquired-intangible amortisation (Red Hat, HashiCorp, Confluent) that is non-cash and largely non-deductible; the cash tax path (18% -> 20%) is calibrated to actual cash taxes (17.3% of EBIT-after-SBC in FY2025) rather than the statutory rate applied to a D&A-shielded EBIT, which is what keeps the shield from being overstated. FY2025 GAAP net income 10,593 carries a 1.4bn Q4 tax benefit -- not used as an anchor. Price is the 28 Sep regular close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at the bottom of the trimmed guide; FY2027-28 the z17 trough (IBM Z -40% YoY in Q2 2026) coincides with Consulting staying flat as hyperscaler copilots absorb the AI-services budget, and Software slows to mid-single digits as OpenShift matures. Group growth 1-2%. Margin slips 1.5pp on Consulting utilisation and Infrastructure deleverage; SBC stays at 4%+ as retention grants for three acquired software teams roll. Cash tax climbs to 22%. Working capital consumes 5% of growth (financing receivables). Terminal 13x, 2% growth. No solvency issue -- 55bn net debt is investment-grade -- but no deleveraging either.

base.narrative: FY2026 at the midpoint of the 4-5% cc guide (Confluent included), then organic 3-3.5% fading to 2.5% as the z17 cycle troughs in FY2027 and Software carries the mix. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands 1pp over the decade on Software mix (44% -> ~50% of revenue). SBC held near the elevated post-HashiCorp/Confluent level, gliding only 0.7pp. Cash tax rises to 20% with Pillar Two. Terminal 15x owner FCF (the cap binds; Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would give 20.5x).

bull.narrative: GenAI book of business (>12.5bn ITD) converts into recognised Consulting revenue and Consulting returns to mid-single-digit growth; Red Hat/OpenShift (+30% ARR) plus HashiCorp and Confluent keep Software at low-double-digit growth so the group compounds 5% for four years; z17 tail plus the compact/rack-mount configurations cushion the FY2027 mainframe trough. Software mix lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin 3pp to 30.5%. Deferred-revenue growth captures 5% of the revenue increase. Terminal 16x.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up because: 55bn net debt (3.4x net debt/EBITDA after Confluent) makes the equity a levered claim on a 2-4% grower, FY2026 guidance was already trimmed mid-year, Q2 2026 printed +1% revenue with Consulting flat and IBM Z -40%, and SBC is rising faster than cash flow. Bull down because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- AI-consulting conversion, sustained double-digit Software growth through three acquisition integrations, and a benign mainframe trough. No going-concern or single-regulator risk, so bear is not pushed higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
